GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS

These General Terms and Conditions are incorporated into and made a part of the Cover Agreement between the Parties. Capitalized terms used here have the meanings given in the Cover Agreement or below.
CONTRACT DOCUMENTS

Contract Documents. The Cover Agreement, these General Terms and Conditions, the other Exhibits, all written Change Orders, and any other documents the Parties expressly identify in writing are collectively referred to as the “Contract Documents.” The Contractor shall perform the Work described in the Contract Documents.

Incorporation by Reference. Plans, proposals, estimates, specifications, and approved selections that are identified in an Exhibit or a Change Order are incorporated into this Agreement by reference. Documents not so identified are not part of the Contract Documents.

Order of Precedence. If there is a conflict among the Contract Documents, the following order of precedence controls: first, a fully executed Change Order (later-dated over earlier-dated); second, these General Terms and Conditions; third, the Cover Agreement; and fourth, the other Exhibits.
SCOPE OF WORK

Work Included. The Contractor shall furnish the labor, materials, equipment, tools, supervision, and services reasonably necessary to complete the Work described in the Scope of Work described in Exhibit B, in accordance with the Contract Documents and applicable law.

Work Excluded. Any work, material, or service that is not specifically included in the Scope of Work is excluded from this Agreement unless it is added by a written Change Order. Without limiting the foregoing, the Contractor is not responsible for work outside the Scope of Work, for correcting deficiencies in work performed by others, or for conditions the Contractor did not create.

Cutting, Patching, and Site Cleanliness. The Contractor is responsible for cutting, fitting, or patching required to complete the Work, and, where applicable, for reasonably matching the quality, performance, and finish of existing adjacent surfaces. The Contractor shall keep the Premises reasonably free from accumulation of debris and trash related to the Work, and, upon completion, shall remove its tools, equipment, and surplus material and properly dispose of waste materials.
THE OWNER IS RESPONSIBLE FOR REVIEWING THE SCOPE OF WORK, PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS, AND SELECTIONS AND FOR CONFIRMING THAT THEY REFLECT THE OWNER’S INTENT BEFORE THE WORK BEGINS.
CONTRACT PRICE

Pricing Method. Except where the Parties execute a separate Cost-Plus or Time-and-Materials Rider that expressly supersedes this Section and Exhibit C, the “Contract Price” stated in the Cover Agreement and Exhibit C is a fixed price for the Work. The Contract Price includes the allowances identified in Exhibit D and may be adjusted only as expressly permitted by the Contract Documents, including through Change Orders and the provisions addressing concealed conditions, code-required work, delays, and changes in materials or selections.
Adjustments to the Contract Price. The Contract Price is subject to adjustment, by written Change Order or as otherwise provided in this Agreement, for each of the following:
changes in the Work requested by the Owner;
concealed or unforeseen conditions as described in this Agreement;
work required by applicable code that could not reasonably have been identified before the Work began;
changes in materials or products, including unavailability, discontinuation, or substantial price increases;
changes to the Owner’s selections or allowances;
delays or interference not attributable to the Contractor; and
other conditions outside the Contractor’s reasonable control.

Taxes. Except as otherwise stated in the Contract Price and Payment Schedule, the Contract Price includes applicable sales, use, and similar taxes on materials and equipment furnished by the Contractor.
DEPOSIT, PROGRESS PAYMENTS, AND FINAL PAYMENT

Payment Schedule. The Owner shall pay the Contractor the Contract Price in accordance with the deposit, progress-payment, and final-payment schedule set out in the Contract Price and Payment Schedule. Progress payments are earned when the applicable milestone is substantially achieved, and are not contingent on completion of every minor item on the Punch List associated with that milestone.

Deposit. The Owner shall pay the deposit stated in the Cover Agreement or the Contract Price and Payment Schedule upon execution of this Agreement or before the Work begins. The deposit shall be applied against the Contract Price.

Payment Terms. Each payment is due within ten (10) days after the Contractor notifies the Owner in writing that the payment is due. Any amount not paid when due shall bear interest from the due date until paid at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by North Carolina law.

Suspension for Nonpayment. If the Owner fails to make any payment when due, the Contractor may, after giving the Owner seven (7) days’ written notice and an opportunity to cure, suspend the Work until payment is made. The Contract Time and Contract Price are equitably adjusted for any such suspension, including reasonable remobilization costs.

Title and Freedom from Liens. The Contractor warrants that title to Work for which payment is due will pass to the Owner no later than the time of payment, and that Work for which payment has been received will, to the best of the Contractor’s knowledge, be free and clear of liens, claims, and security interests adverse to the Owner’s interest.

Payment of Subcontractors and Suppliers. Upon receipt of payment from the Owner, the Contractor shall promptly pay each subcontractor and supplier the amount owed for the corresponding portion of the Work. The Owner has no responsibility for payments to a subcontractor or supplier, except as otherwise required by law.
ALLOWANCES AND SELECTIONS

Allowances. Where exact materials, products, or finishes have not been selected when this Agreement is signed, the Contract Price includes the allowances identified in the Selections and Allowances (Exhibit D). Unless that exhibit states otherwise, an allowance covers the cost of the item only and does not include delivery, handling, taxes, installation labor, overhead, or profit, which are included in the Contract Price.

Overage and Credit. If the actual cost of a selected item exceeds its allowance, the Owner pays the difference plus any applicable additional labor, delivery, tax, handling, and other project costs. If the actual cost is less than the allowance, the Owner receives a credit in the amount of the difference for that item.

Selection Deadlines. The Owner is responsible for making selections by the deadlines the Contractor reasonably establishes. Delays caused by late or changed selections extend the project schedule and may increase the Contract Price as provided in this Agreement.
CHANGE ORDERS

Written Authorization Required. Changes to the scope, price, materials, allowances, or schedule of the Work must be authorized in a signed writing in the form of the Exhibit F (each a “Change Order”), before the changed Work is performed, except as provided for emergency and concealed-condition work in this Agreement. A Change Order signed or approved by both Parties is the exclusive means of changing the Contract Documents. Approval given by email, text message, electronic signature, or through the Contractor’s project-management system qualifies as written authorization where legally enforceable.
Matters a Change Order May Address. A Change Order may adjust the Contract Price, the Scope of Work, material selections, allowances, the project schedule, and the completion date, as applicable.

Emergency and Code-Required Work. If emergency work, code-required work, or work arising from a concealed condition is reasonably necessary to protect persons or property or to keep the project moving, the Contractor may proceed and shall promptly notify the Owner and document the change by Change Order. The Contract Price and Contract Time are equitably adjusted for such work.

Disagreement on Price. If the Parties cannot agree on the price of a change, the Contractor shall perform the change on a time-and-material basis at the Contractor’s standard rates plus reasonable overhead and profit, and the Contract Price is adjusted accordingly, without waiving either Party’s other rights.
CONCEALED AND UNFORESEEN CONDITIONS

No Responsibility for Hidden Conditions. The Contractor is not financially responsible for conditions that could not reasonably have been discovered before demolition or construction began. When such a condition is encountered, the Contract Price and Contract Time are subject to equitable adjustment. Concealed or unforeseen conditions include, without limitation, the following:
water damage, moisture intrusion, mold, mildew, rot, or fungal growth;
termite, pest, or vermin damage;
structural deficiencies or inadequate prior construction;
plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or HVAC deficiencies;
hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, and similar substances;
underground, site, soil, drainage, or utility conditions;
code violations in existing construction; and
unexpected framing, foundation, or mechanical conditions.

Hazardous Materials. The Contractor is not responsible for the presence, handling, removal, or remediation of hazardous materials at the Premises. If a hazardous-materials condition requires remediation, the Owner is responsible for the cost, and the Contract Time and Contract Price are equitably adjusted for any resulting shutdown, delay, or start-up.
SCHEDULE AND DELAYS

Estimates. The period from the estimated start date to the estimated Substantial Completion date stated in the Cover Agreement is the “Contract Time.” Project schedules and estimated completion dates are good-faith estimates and are not guarantees unless a specific date is expressly stated to be guaranteed in the Contract Price and Payment Schedule.
Excusable Delays. The Contractor is entitled to a reasonable extension of the schedule, without liability, for delays outside its reasonable control, including delays caused by:
weather and unavoidable casualties;
inspections and permitting;
material delays, shortages, and backorders;
labor or subcontractor availability;
Owner-requested changes and Owner selection delays;
concealed or unforeseen conditions;
utility interruptions;
governmental actions or orders; and
other events beyond the Contractor’s reasonable control.
Notice. The Contractor shall give the Owner reasonable notice of a material delay and its expected effect on the schedule.
PERMITS AND INSPECTIONS

Responsibility. The Scope of Work identifies which Party is responsible for obtaining and paying for permits and governmental fees. Where the Contractor obtains permits, the Owner shall promptly provide the information, documentation, and access reasonably necessary for approvals.

Code-Required Changes. Work required by an authority having jurisdiction that is outside the original Scope of Work is treated as additional work by Change Order when it could not reasonably have been anticipated.

Inspections. The Contractor shall arrange for inspections required by the Contract Documents or by law at the appropriate times and shall provide the Owner with copies of permits and inspection approvals upon request.
OWNER RESPONSIBILITIES
Owner’s Obligations. In addition to the Owner’s other obligations under this Agreement, the Owner shall:
provide the Contractor with reasonable and safe access to the Premises during the Work;
make selections and give approvals in a timely manner;
make payments when due;
remove or protect furniture, valuables, and other personal property as the Contractor reasonably instructs;
provide water, electricity, and other utilities at the Premises when reasonably required for the Work;
keep children, pets, and unauthorized persons away from construction areas;
disclose known conditions of the Premises that may affect the Work, including the location of concealed utilities and known hazards; and
obtain homeowners’ association and architectural-review approvals, unless obtaining those approvals is expressly included in the Contractor’s Scope of Work.
Owner Information. The Contractor is entitled to rely on the accuracy and completeness of information the Owner provides for the Project.
SUBCONTRACTORS; MEANS AND METHODS

Use of Subcontractors. The Contractor may use qualified subcontractors and suppliers to perform portions of the Work. The Contractor remains responsible to the Owner for the performance of the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents.

Means and Methods. The Contractor is solely responsible for, and has control over, the construction means, methods, techniques, sequences, and procedures, and for coordinating all portions of the Work and its subcontractors.
MATERIALS AND SUBSTITUTIONS

Substitutions. When a specified material or product becomes unavailable, is discontinued, is subject to excessive delay, or otherwise becomes impractical to obtain, the Contractor may substitute a commercially reasonable equivalent, subject to the Owner’s approval where the substitution is material. The Owner’s approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

Natural Variation. Natural materials, including wood, stone, tile, and similar products, may vary in color, grain, texture, veining, and pattern. Reasonable variation is characteristic of these materials and is not a defect.

Manufacturer Warranties. The Contractor is not responsible for manufacturer defects beyond the applicable manufacturer warranties. Manufacturer warranties pass through to the Owner where they are transferable.
Owner Supplied Materials. If the Owner elects to supply materials, products, fixtures, or appliances for the Work, the following apply:
the Contractor does not warrant Owner-supplied items and is not responsible for their design, quality, fitness, or performance;
the Contractor is not responsible for delays, defects, missing parts, incorrect measurements, incompatibility, damage, shortages, or replacement costs associated with Owner-supplied items;
additional labor, handling, return trips, or rework caused by Owner-supplied items is chargeable to the Owner as additional work; and
the Owner is responsible for timely delivery of Owner-supplied items to the Premises.
WORKMANSHIP WARRANTY

Limited Warranty. The Contractor warrants to the Owner that the Work will be performed in a good and workmanlike manner and will be free from defects in workmanship for a period of one (1) year after Substantial Completion of the Work.
Exclusions. The workmanship warranty does not cover, and the Contractor is not responsible for:
normal wear and tear;
damage caused by the Owner or others;
abuse, misuse, or improper operation;
lack of, or improper, maintenance;
manufacturer defects in products and materials;
movement, settlement, shrinkage, or expansion outside the Contractor’s Work;
work modified, repaired, or maintained by parties other than the Contractor; and
conditions outside the Contractor’s reasonable control.

Manufacturer Warranties Pass-Through. Warranties provided by manufacturers and suppliers pass through to the Owner where transferable, and the Owner’s recourse for a product defect is against the manufacturer or supplier under the applicable warranty.

Disclaimer. Except for the express warranty stated in this Article, and to the fullest extent permitted by law, the Contractor disclaims all other warranties, whether express or implied, including any implied warranty of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.
SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION AND PUNCH LIST

Substantial Completion. The Work is substantially complete when it is sufficiently complete for the Owner to use it for its intended purpose (“Substantial Completion”). When the Contractor considers the Work substantially complete, the express warranty commences and the Contractor prepares and submits to the Owner a list of items to be completed or corrected (the “Punch List”).

Walkthrough and Punch List. The Owner shall promptly conduct a walkthrough with the Contractor and identify any additional items to be completed or corrected. After the Parties agree on the Punch List, the Contractor shall promptly complete or correct the legitimate items on that list.

Final Payment and Minor Items. Minor items on the Punch List do not permit the Owner to withhold the entire final payment. The Owner may withhold from final payment only a reasonable amount, not to exceed 150% of the reasonable cost to complete or correct the remaining items on the Punch List, until those items are completed or corrected.

Lien Waivers. The Contractor shall submit with its final invoice a conditional final lien waiver covering the Work and conditioned upon the Contractor’s receipt of the final payment in finally collected funds. Upon the Owner’s reasonable request, the Contractor shall also provide conditional final lien waivers from subcontractors and suppliers whose amounts are included in the final invoice. Final payment may not be withheld or delayed based on the absence of an unconditional lien waiver. Promptly after receiving the final payment in finally collected funds, the Contractor shall provide the Owner with an unconditional final lien waiver. The Contractor shall also use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and provide unconditional final lien waivers from requested subcontractors and suppliers after the Contractor has paid them in full.
SUSPENSION AND TERMINATION

Contractor’s Right to Suspend or Terminate. In addition to the Contractor’s suspension right for nonpayment, the Contractor may suspend or, after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure, terminate the Work for:
nonpayment;
unsafe conditions at the Premises;
Owner interference with the Work;
the Owner’s failure to provide access;
the Owner’s material breach of this Agreement; and
other circumstances that make continued performance unreasonable or unlawful.

Owner Termination for Cause. The Owner may terminate this Agreement if the Contractor is in substantial breach and fails to cure the breach within a reasonable time, not less than ten (10) days, after written notice describing the breach.

Owner Termination Without Cause. If the Owner terminates the Work other than for the Contractor’s uncured default, the Owner shall pay the Contractor for: (a) Work performed through the date of termination, including reasonable overhead and profit; (b) materials ordered or delivered and other commitments reasonably made for the Work; (c) demobilization costs; and (d) other costs and damages reasonably incurred by reason of the termination.
PROTECTION OF PERSONS AND PROPERTY; INSURANCE AND RISK OF LOSS

Protection of Persons and Property. The Contractor shall take commercially reasonable precautions to prevent damage, injury, or loss to persons and to property at or adjacent to the Premises arising from the Work, and shall promptly remedy damage or loss caused by the Contractor or by anyone for whose acts the Contractor is responsible.

Contractor’s Insurance. The Contractor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance and other coverage customary for its business and required by law, including workers’ compensation at statutory limits and, where applicable, commercial automobile liability. Upon the Owner’s request, the Contractor shall provide a certificate of insurance.

Owner’s Insurance. The Owner shall maintain the Owner’s usual homeowners’ or property insurance and shall provide property insurance sufficient to cover the replacement value of the Owner’s existing property that is not otherwise covered by any builder’s risk insurance for the project.

Builder’s Risk. For larger projects, such as substantial additions or projects involving significant new construction, the Party identified in the Contract Price and Payment Schedule shall provide builder’s risk insurance covering the Work on a replacement-cost basis until Substantial Completion.

Waiver of Subrogation. To the extent a loss is covered by property or builder’s risk insurance, and unless the applicable policy prohibits the waiver, the Owner and the Contractor waive all rights against each other and their respective subcontractors, suppliers, agents, and employees for that loss, except as to the proceeds of the insurance.
Preexisting Conditions. The Contractor is not responsible for loss or damage arising from preexisting conditions at the Premises that are not caused by the Contractor’s Work.
INDEMNIFICATION

Each Party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other Party from and against third-party claims for bodily injury or damage to tangible property to the extent caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of the indemnifying Party or those for whom it is responsible. Neither Party is required to indemnify the other against the other’s own negligence. This indemnity is mutual and limited to comply with North Carolina law governing construction indemnity clauses.
LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

To the fullest extent permitted by law, neither Party is liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, or punitive damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including lost profits, loss of use, and diminution in value. The Contractor’s total liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement is limited to the Contract Price paid to the Contractor for the project giving rise to the claim. This Article does not limit either Party’s obligations under the Insurance or Indemnification Articles, or liability that cannot be limited under applicable law.
DISPUTE RESOLUTION

The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement through good-faith discussion between the Parties. If the dispute is not resolved by discussion, the Parties shall submit the dispute to non-binding mediation administered in Wake County, North Carolina, before a mutually acceptable mediator, as a condition precedent to arbitration, except as provided below. If mediation does not resolve the dispute, the dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Construction Industry Arbitration Rules, seated in Wake County, North Carolina. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Contractor may at any time pursue and enforce its statutory lien and collection remedies, seek to perfect or enforce a claim of lien, and bring an action to recover unpaid amounts, without first satisfying the discussion, mediation, or arbitration requirements.
LIENS, COLLECTION, AND ATTORNEY FEES

Lien Rights Preserved. The Contractor reserves and does not waive any lien or bond rights available under North Carolina law. Nothing in this Agreement constitutes an advance waiver or release of those rights. Any lien waiver or release shall be provided only in accordance with Section 14.4 and shall be effective solely to the extent, for the period, and upon the conditions expressly stated in the waiver or release.

Notice to Lien Agent. Where required by North Carolina law the Owner shall designate a lien agent and provide the Contractor and, upon request, the Contractor’s subcontractors and suppliers, with the lien agent’s contact information.

Attorney Fees and Collection Costs. To the extent enforceable, the Owner is responsible for the reasonable attorney fees, collection costs, and other costs the Contractor incurs to collect amounts properly owed under this Agreement.
PHOTOGRAPHY AND MARKETING

The Owner authorizes the Contractor to photograph and video-record the Work and the completed project and to use those images, without further approval or compensation, for project documentation, its portfolio, website, social media, advertising, and other marketing purposes. Without the Owner’s separate consent, the Contractor shall not disclose the Owner’s name or street address or intentionally depict the Owner or other occupants, personal documents, security features, or private areas unrelated to the Work.
COMMUNICATIONS AND NOTICES

Electronic Communications. Email, electronic signatures, text messages, and the Contractor’s project-management software qualify as written communication and written authorization where legally enforceable.

Notices. Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective when delivered by hand, by a nationally recognized courier, by certified mail (return receipt requested), or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses stated in the Cover Agreement or to another address a Party designates in writing.
NORTH CAROLINA NOTICES AND DISCLOSURES
Licensing. The Contractor is licensed as a general contractor by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors, License #109080.

Homeowners Recovery Fund. For the construction or alteration of a single-family residential dwelling unit for which a building permit is obtained, North Carolina maintains a Homeowners Recovery Fund administered by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors to reimburse homeowners for certain reimbursable losses caused by a licensed general contractor’s dishonest or incompetent conduct. Information is available from the Board.

Right to Cancel. If this Agreement constitutes a home-solicitation or door-to-door sale subject to applicable North Carolina or federal law, the Owner may cancel the transaction within the period and in the manner stated in the Notice of Cancellation furnished by the Contractor (see Exhibit G).
GENERAL PROVISIONS

Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. The exclusive venue for any permitted litigation is the state and federal courts located in Wake County, North Carolina.

Entire Agreement. The Contract Documents constitute the entire and integrated agreement between the Parties and supersede all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral. This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument or Change Order signed or electronically approved by both Parties.

Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, that provision is enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law and the remaining provisions continue in full force and effect.
Waiver. A Party’s failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of that provision or of the right to enforce it later. A waiver is effective only if in writing and signed by the waiving Party.

Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s written consent, except that the Contractor may assign to an affiliate or a successor to its business, and either Party may collaterally assign its rights to a lender. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

Survival. Sections 14.4, 15.3, 16.5, and 16.6, together with Articles 4, 13, and 17 through 24, survive Substantial Completion and any expiration or termination of this Agreement. Expiration or termination does not affect any right, remedy, payment obligation, claim, or liability that accrued before the effective date of expiration or termination.
Counterparts and Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one agreement.
Independent Counsel. Each Party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to review this Agreement with legal counsel of its choosing and enters into it voluntarily.
